title: Coconut-Turmeric Chicken
description: A golden, fragrant one-pot chicken dinner where turmeric and ginger bloom in oil before getting softened by a full can of coconut milk. Searing the chicken first builds a fond that makes the sauce taste like it simmered all day.

steps.text: Season chicken pieces generously with salt. Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken in a single layer and sear until golden on the underside, about 4 minutes. Flip and cook another 2 minutes — the chicken doesn't need to be cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion to the same pot and cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander, cumin, and cayenne. Stir constantly until fragrant and the spices coat the onions evenly, about 1 minute.

Pour in coconut milk and fish sauce, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer, then return the chicken and any collected juices. Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly, 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice. Taste for salt. Serve over jasmine rice, topped with cilantro.

inspirations.author: Kay Chun
inspirations.note: Inspired by the broader NYT and BA tradition of quick coconut-milk curries, drawing on Southeast Asian flavor profiles
